name: Chen Yiy Hwuan
current_role: Chief Executive Officer – Hotels, NagaCorp Ltd (appointed April 2022; latest status not confirmed)
profile: Son of the late NagaCorp founder Chen Lip Keong (d. Dec 2023), whose HK-listed company runs the NagaWorld casino-resort monopoly in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. His wealth comes from the family's NagaCorp stake. In April 2022 he was named CEO – Hotels as part of a succession reshuffle; his brother Chen Yiy Fon now leads the group.
interesting_fact: When the 2022 succession plan split NagaCorp's CEO role into four, he (then 42) was named CEO of hotels alongside two of his brothers as joint CEOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO – Hotels he oversaw NagaFarm Limited, NagaCorp's wholly owned sustainable-agriculture subsidiary that grows food for the Naga 1 and Naga 2 hotels.
notes: Low public profile; little personal press. IR email reported on NagaCorp's IR enquiries page (page was unreachable for direct re-check). Best route is via NagaCorp IR. Current title after 2024 management changes not confirmed.

name: Wei Jinkun
current_role: Major shareholder (~19%) of Weaver Network Technology (泛微网络, SSE: 603039), maker of the e-cology OA platform
profile: Wei Jinkun (韦锦坤) is the second-largest shareholder of Shanghai-based Weaver Network, a collaboration/office-automation software firm founded in 2001 by Wei Lidong whose flagship product is e-cology; it listed in Shanghai in January 2017. His wealth comes from this stake. Little else is publicly documented about him.
interesting_fact: In 2020 he agreed to transfer about 5% of Weaver Network to Tencent's industrial investment fund, bringing Tencent in as a strategic shareholder.
notes: Matched via 'E-cology' = Weaver's flagship OA product; shareholder data from 10jqka (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/603039/holder.html). Relationship to founder Wei Lidong not confirmed. Very private; route would be via Weaver Network (weaver.com.cn) board secretary/IR.

name: Vitaly Orlov
current_role: CEO, co-founder and sole owner, Norebo Holding (Murmansk, Russia)
profile: Murmansk-born (1965) Orlov co-founded Norebo, Russia's largest vertically integrated seafood company, after starting in the late 1990s by supplying used trawlers to Russian fishermen in exchange for fish. Norebo has spent ~$600m buying fishing companies and catches ~400,000 tons of cod, haddock and pollock a year; since 2022 he has also bought shipyards and port terminals.
interesting_fact: He moved to Norway in 1996 and lived there until 2014, then gave up his Norwegian citizenship when he moved back to Murmansk.
deep_cut_fact: His English skills launched his career: after working in the fleet he joined the Sevryba fishing authority's export-contracts department, then in 1993 joined Swedish seafood exporter Scansea International's Murmansk office before moving to its Norway office in 1996.
notes: Sensitive: Norebo was sanctioned by the EU (May 2025) and Norway (July 2025); Orlov is suing Norway and The Barents Observer (defamation, London). Expect a guarded, lawyered response; contact via Norebo media office.

name: Huxiong Chen
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and President, Shanghai M&G Stationery Inc. (晨光股份, SSE: 603899)
profile: Chen Huxiong (陈湖雄, b. 1970, Shantou) started out selling imported stationery around China, became a China agent for Japanese and Korean brands, and launched the M&G own brand in Shanghai after the 1997 Asian financial crisis hit his suppliers. M&G grew into China's largest stationery maker via a vast school-side retail network. He co-owns it with his twin brother Chen Huwen (chairman) and sister.
interesting_fact: M&G was born out of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: when the Japanese and Korean stationery firms he distributed for went bust, he decided to build his own brand.
deep_cut_fact: He left school for work at 17 in 1987 as a toy-factory operator earning 50 yuan a month; as a travelling salesman he once stood for 54 hours on a green-skin train from Shijiazhuang to Chengdu. Selling to Xinhua Bookstores got him into stationery.
notes: Low-profile; few English interviews. Best route is M&G's board-secretary/IR office (ir@mg-pen.com, published in annual report summary).

name: Hubert d'Ornano
current_role: Deceased (25 September 2015); co-founder of Sisley Paris
profile: Count Hubert d'Ornano (1926–2015) co-founded Sisley, the French luxury skincare house, in 1976 with his wife Isabelle; earlier he co-founded Jean d'Albret and Orlane. He died on 25 September 2015 aged 89. Sisley is now run by his family (son Philippe as chairman).
notes: Died 25 Sept 2015 (WWD obituary https://wwd.com/feature/sisley-hubert-dornano-dies-at-10242826/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_d%27Ornano). Fortune now with widow Isabelle and children; for a Sisley angle, approach Philippe d'Ornano / Sisley corporate press instead.

name: Kapeng Zhang
current_role: Chairman and President, Weixing Group (伟星集团), controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Weixing New Building Materials (002372) and Zhejiang Weixing Industrial (002003)
profile: Zhang Kapeng (章卡鹏, b. 1965, Linhai, Zhejiang) rose from factory worker to chairman of Weixing Group, a Linhai conglomerate spanning garment accessories (buttons, zippers), plastic piping, property and finance. With partner Zhang Sanyun he jointly controls two listed firms: Weixing New Materials, a leading PP-R pipe maker, and Weixing Co., China's top button and zipper maker.
interesting_fact: Weixing New Materials' PP-R pipes were used in landmark projects including Beijing's Bird's Nest, the Water Cube and the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the group's predecessor, the Linhai plexiglass factory, at 17 as an ordinary worker, was mentored personally by founder Ming Pibai from 1985, and became chairman at 35 in 2000. He was named a 2021-22 National Outstanding Entrepreneur.
notes: Current role confirmed by Weixing Co. 2025 annual report summary (Apr 2026). IR email is for Weixing Co. (002003), where he is a 5.58% shareholder; Weixing New Materials (002372) has its own board secretary. Bio details from a secondary Chinese brand site (cnpp.cn).

name: Reshma Shetty
current_role: Co-founder, President and Board Director, Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA); handed COO duties to others from 1 Jan 2026
profile: Reshma Shetty co-founded synthetic-biology platform Ginkgo Bioworks in 2008 with fellow MIT researchers and served as President and COO until the end of 2025. Her fortune stems from her stake in Ginkgo, which listed on the NYSE via SPAC in 2021. She remains President and a director, and has served on the U.S. Defense Science Board since 2022.
interesting_fact: Ginkgo was the first biotech company to go through Y Combinator (2014); BIO gave Shetty its Rosalind Franklin Award for Leadership in Industrial Biotechnology in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Before biology she earned a B.S. in computer science at the University of Utah; as an MIT PhD student she co-organized the first international synthetic biology conference (SB1.0) in 2004.
notes: Role change per Ginkgo 8-K of 23 Dec 2025. Speaks publicly fairly often (university seminars, R&D World interview on autonomous labs) - relevant for a data/AI-lab angle. Route via Ginkgo press office.
